Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

atmosphere noun

the mood of a place or a gathering

also mood (of a place), ambience, a cheerful atmosphere, a gloomy atmosphere

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.243: hilaritātis plēnum jūdicium ac laetitiae fuit (Lewis & Short)

hilaritās, hilaritātis f.

noun, third declension

a cheerful atmosphere, good humour

Latin has no word for an atmosphere as such: it names the mood that fills a place, as Cicero says a trial was “full of good humour and gladness”. hilaritās is cheerfulness in a person (Cic. Off. 1.108) and, in Columella, fine weather (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • tristitia, tristitiae f. — a gloomy atmosphere, gloom

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.40.3: hanc tristitiam temporum (Lewis & Short)

    Sadness in a person, and the gloom of times, places and skies (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • itaque hilaritātis plēnum jūdicium ac laetitiae fuit

    and so the whole court was full of good humour and gladnessCic. de Or. 1.243 (Lewis & Short)

  • hilaritātem illam, quā hanc tristitiam temporum condiēbāmus, in perpetuum āmīsī

    I have lost for ever the cheerfulness with which we used to season the gloom of these timesCic. Att. 12.40.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also be in a good mood, air, peace.
